core_obligations: Set up Serre's criterion (proof lines 3783-3792): completion on finite modules is exact because it is given by tensoring with the flat completion of the base, and by Serre's criterion it suffices to verify the conditions (S2) and (R1) for the local rings of the completion of the subalgebra, for primes lying over primes of the subalgebra.

Condition (S2) (proof lines 3794-3812): if the prime of the subalgebra has dimension at least two then its depth is at least two, and flatness of the completion map gives the same depth bound for the local ring of the completion; if the dimension is at most one the local ring is a discrete valuation ring or a field, and the larger algebra is faithfully flat over it, so after completion and localization one descends the condition from the completion of the larger algebra.

Condition (R1) (proof lines 3814-3820): it suffices to consider primes of the completion of the subalgebra of dimension at most one; by the dimension formula the corresponding prime of the subalgebra also has dimension at most one, and the same faithfully flatness allows one to descend the regularity condition from the completion of the larger algebra, which completes the verification of Serre's criterion.
proof_roadmap: Reduce by Serre's criterion to verifying (S2) and (R1) for the completion of the subalgebra.
Use depth and flatness in the high dimensional case, and faithful flatness of the larger algebra in the low dimensional case, to get (S2).
Use the dimension formula and the same faithful flatness to get (R1).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for finite algebras over a local Noetherian ring, normality of the smaller algebra together with normality of the completion of the larger one implies normality of the completion of the smaller one (statement lines 3775-3781). The proof (proof lines 3783-3824) applies Serre's criterion, verifying the conditions (S2) and (R1) for the local rings of the completion through depth and flatness arguments in high dimension and faithful flatness of the larger algebra in low dimension. H3: a criterion verification with a two-case analysis, written out in full.
